title: Learning for Safety-Critical Control with Control Barrier Functions
authors: Andrew Taylor and Andrew Singletary and Yisong Yue and Aaron Ames
summary: Learns the effect of model uncertainty on control barrier conditions and iteratively updates a safety controller. Simulation and Segway experiments demonstrate the value of adapting the model used for safety enforcement.
gap: A barrier protects the safety conditions encoded by its designer. This motivates specifying human contact and object-related hazards explicitly, while retaining a common low-level shield across comparisons.
extra: The cited proceedings publication is June 2020; its earlier preprint was released in 2019. Inclusion follows publication year.

title: Recovery RL: Safe Reinforcement Learning with Learned Recovery Zones
authors: Brijen Thananjeyan and Ashwin Balakrishna and Suraj Nair and Michael Luo and Krishnan Srinivasan and Minho Hwang and Joseph E. Gonzalez and Julian Ibarz and Chelsea Finn and Ken Goldberg
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters; ICRA presentation
summary: Separates a reward-seeking task policy from a learned recovery policy. Offline constraint-violation data support a safety critic and recovery behavior; evaluation includes contact-rich manipulation and a physical robot.
gap: Separating task and recovery policies is established. The proposed study must show better selection and execution of recovery under coupled human, object, and humanoid dynamics.

title: Safety and Liveness Guarantees through Reach-Avoid Reinforcement Learning
authors: Kai-Chieh Hsu and Vicenc Rubies-Royo and Claire Tomlin and Jaime F. Fisac
summary: Develops a discounted reach-avoid Bellman formulation and uses approximate learned solutions within a supervisory framework. It connects reaching a desired condition to avoiding failure along the path.
gap: A safe final posture is insufficient when the transition collides with a person or drops an object. Reach-avoid structure motivates evaluating the complete intervention trajectory.

title: Safe Learning in Robotics: From Learning-Based Control to Safe Reinforcement Learning
authors: Lukas Brunke and Melissa Greeff and Adam W. Hall and Zhaocong Yuan and Siqi Zhou and Jacopo Panerati and Angela P. Schoellig
venue: Annual Review of Control Robotics and Autonomous Systems
summary: Surveys control and reinforcement-learning approaches to safe decision making under uncertainty, separating performance improvement, robustness, and certification. It emphasizes realistic benchmarks and shared terminology.
gap: Provides the vocabulary for stating what is assumed, monitored, and empirically demonstrated. A finite simulation study supports a bounded safety claim, not universal safe deployment.

title: Safe-Control-Gym: A Unified Benchmark Suite for Safe Learning-Based Control and Reinforcement Learning in Robotics
authors: Zhaocong Yuan and Adam W. Hall and Siqi Zhou and Lukas Brunke and Melissa Greeff and Jacopo Panerati and Angela P. Schoellig
summary: Introduces common environments, dynamics interfaces, constraints, and repeatable disturbances for comparing control and reinforcement-learning approaches. Its systems include cart-pole and quadrotors.
gap: The transferable lesson is experimental discipline: share dynamics, observations, disturbances, and constraints. The benchmark itself is not a humanoid interruption benchmark.

title: Safe Control With Learned Certificates: A Survey of Neural Lyapunov, Barrier, and Contraction Methods for Robotics and Control
authors: Charles Dawson and Sicun Gao and Chuchu Fan
summary: Reviews learned certificates for safety and stability, including verification and their use during policy learning. It explains how a learned model can be connected to mathematical conditions.
gap: A calibrated risk predictor is not automatically a barrier certificate. The workshop paper should claim empirical risk reduction unless its dynamics, uncertainty, and verification assumptions justify a theorem.

title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances
authors: Michael Ahn and others
summary: Combines language-based task relevance with the affordances of pretrained robot skills. Real mobile-manipulation experiments demonstrate how language instructions can be grounded in executable actions.
gap: Skill feasibility is essential but does not by itself establish safety during interruption. Use a grounded skill interface and keep the language planner outside the fast safety loop.

title: Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models
authors: Wenlong Huang and others
summary: Feeds success signals, scene descriptions, and human feedback back into a language-model planner. Closed-loop feedback improves instruction completion in simulated and real manipulation settings.
gap: Task repair through feedback motivates resumption after interruption. Completion improvements alone cannot establish reduced human contact or safe switching dynamics.

title: Robots That Ask For Help: Uncertainty Alignment for Large Language Model Planners
authors: Allen Z. Ren and Anushri Dixit and Alexandra Bodrova and Sumeet Singh and Stephen Tu and Noah Brown and Peng Xu and Leila Takayama and Fei Xia and Jake Varley and Zhenjia Xu and Dorsa Sadigh and Andy Zeng and Anirudha Majumdar
summary: KnowNo calibrates language-planner uncertainty with conformal prediction and asks for help when ambiguity requires it. Its guarantees concern task completion under specified conditions and human assistance.
gap: Uncertainty should influence intervention, but asking or waiting also consumes physical time. Planning-confidence guarantees cannot be transferred directly to collision-free humanoid recovery.

title: Closing the Loop on Runtime Monitors with Fallback-Safe MPC
authors: Rohan Sinha and Edward Schmerling and Marco Pavone
venue: IEEE Conference on Decision and Control
summary: Maintains a feasible fallback while using learned perception, and calibrates monitoring to detect perception degradation. The framework connects monitor assumptions to controller tolerance and conditional safety.
gap: Preserving a fallback before failure is established. The proposed extension concerns coupled humanoid, object, and human outcomes during switching, including what happens when no modeled response is feasible.

title: Real-Time Anomaly Detection and Reactive Planning with Large Language Models
authors: Rohan Sinha and Amine Elhafsi and Christopher Agia and Matthew Foutter and Edward Schmerling and Marco Pavone
summary: AESOP combines a fast anomaly classifier and slower semantic reasoning with a predictive controller that maintains fallback options while reasoning takes place. It explicitly accounts for language-model latency.
gap: Latency-aware fallback selection is already prior art. The new contribution must demonstrate why contact transitions and carried-object consequences require more than latency handling alone.

title: ResSafe: Learning Safety Filtering with Residual Reinforcement Learning for Humanoids
authors: Gechen Qu and Tong Zhang and Bike Zhang and Yen-Jen Wang and Koushil Sreenath and Claire Tomlin and Jason Jangho Choi
summary: Learns residual corrections to a nominal humanoid policy, separating tracking performance from safety optimization. The author project evaluates balance tasks and payload conditions.
gap: Payload-aware robustness and performance-safety trade-offs are already studied. Reduced falls do not establish safe outcomes for bystanders or released objects; measure these separately.
extra: Abstract and author project checked; no claim that this review independently verified all experiments. Project: https://sciautonomy.github.io/ResSafe_Web/.

title: HOVER: Versatile Neural Whole-Body Controller for Humanoid Robots
authors: Tairan He and Wenli Xiao and Toru Lin and Zhengyi Luo and Zhenjia Xu and Zhenyu Jiang and Jan Kautz and Changliu Liu and Guanya Shi and Xiaolong Wang and Linxi Fan and Yuke Zhu
venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation
summary: Distills multiple whole-body command modes into a common humanoid controller, supporting transitions among locomotion and manipulation interfaces.
gap: Provides a possible reusable control foundation, not a plug-and-play safety supervisor or proof of grasp competence. Verify robot, checkpoint, command-mode, and manipulation compatibility before committing.
extra: First preprint 2024; conference publication 2025. Code/checkpoint suitability for this study remains an implementation gate.

title: ASAP: Aligning Simulation and Real-World Physics for Learning Agile Humanoid Whole-Body Skills
authors: Tairan He and others
summary: Uses real-world rollout data to learn residual action corrections and align simulation with robot dynamics. It evaluates transfer between simulators and to a Unitree G1.
gap: Shows why simulated impact or recovery improvements require sensitivity checks and cannot automatically establish hardware safety. A second physics configuration is useful, but is not equivalent to hardware validation.

title: SPARK: Safe Protective and Assistive Robot Kit
authors: Yifan Sun and Rui Chen and Kai S. Yun and Yikuan Fang and Sebin Jung and Feihan Li and Bowei Li and Weiye Zhao and Changliu Liu
summary: Provides modular safety constraints, control algorithms, simulation comparisons, and hardware interfaces, including Unitree G1 examples.
gap: Offers relevant infrastructure and baseline implementations. A secondary-harm interruption suite would be an extension with new contact and object-state validation, not an existing SPARK benchmark result.
extra: Cited revision January 14 2026, within cutoff. Repository: https://github.com/intelligent-control-lab/spark.

title: Dexterous Safe Control for Humanoids in Cluttered Environments via Projected Safe Set Algorithm
authors: Rui Chen and Yifan Sun and Changliu Liu
summary: p-SSA handles many limb-level external and self-collision constraints by relaxing conflicts to retain feasible control. It is evaluated in simulation and on a Unitree G1.
gap: A strong geometric-control comparator is needed. Constraint relaxation can admit violations; neither feasibility nor collision avoidance of modeled links proves safe handling of an unstable payload.

title: Learning Safe-Stoppability Monitors for Humanoid Robots
authors: Yifan Sun and Yiyuan Pan and Shangtao Li and Caiwu Ding and Tao Cui and Lingyun Wang and Changliu Liu
summary: PRISM learns whether a fixed fallback reaches a minimum-risk condition without failure, using targeted sampling. Its G1 study includes grasping, transporting, and releasing an object; stopping collisions are explicitly considered.
gap: Do not claim that prior work ignores unsafe stops or manipulation. The proposed distinction is selecting among alternatives with explicit object and bystander consequences, and testing complete closed-loop interventions.
extra: Full-text Sections VI-A, VI-B, and VII checked. Cited as the March preprint rather than relying on later conference reporting.

title: Humanoid Safe Stop via Learned Stoppability Value
authors: Junfeng Long and Pieter Abbeel and Koushil Sreenath and Roberto Horowitz and Guanya Shi and C. Karen Liu
summary: Pairs a learned stop policy with stop-probability and reach-avoidance estimates, switching to a damping fallback when the stopping gate fails. The design transfers across upstream behaviors.
gap: A learned stop-versus-fallback gate is already available by September. Compare against this family where implementation permits, and avoid presenting a binary stopping selector as a new contribution.
extra: ArXiv metadata and indexed author project verified; full manuscript could not be retrieved. Claims are restricted to the abstract and project description: https://junfeng-long.github.io/safestop/.

title: Unified Humanoid Fall-Safety Policy from a Few Demonstrations
authors: Zhengjie Xu and Ye Li and Kwan-Yee Lin and Stella X. Yu
venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation
summary: Combines demonstrations, reinforcement learning, and a memory of reactions to address fall prevention, impact mitigation, and recovery in one humanoid policy, with G1 experiments.
gap: The full fall-and-recovery process is an existing safety target. Extend evaluation to collateral effects on people and objects instead of treating lower robot impact alone as the contribution.
extra: First public version November 2025; ICRA 2026 publication verified on author page.

title: VIGOR: Visual Goal-In-Context Inference for Unified Humanoid Fall Safety
authors: Osher Azulay and Zhengjie Xu and Andrew Scheffer and Stella X. Yu
summary: Distills a teacher into a student using egocentric depth and proprioception to coordinate fall mitigation and recovery on varied terrain. Context-dependent perceptual recovery is already central to the method.
gap: Do not claim the first visual or context-aware humanoid recovery method. Focus on interruption of productive tasks, human/object consequence prediction, and causal comparison of response choices.
extra: The October 15 version changed the title to Unified Perceptive Fall Safety for Humanoids. That post-cutoff revision and its expanded results are excluded.

title: SafeAgentBench: A Benchmark for Safe Task Planning of Embodied LLM Agents
authors: Sheng Yin and Xianghe Pang and Yuanzhuo Ding and Menglan Chen and Yutong Bi and Yichen Xiong and Wenhao Huang and Zhen Xiang and Jing Shao and Siheng Chen
summary: Evaluates embodied agents on safe and hazardous instructions in interactive simulation, with execution-level and semantic assessments across 750 tasks.
gap: Its hazard taxonomy informs scenario design. Task rejection and symbolic execution metrics do not directly quantify impact impulses or balance during humanoid recovery; a physics-grounded endpoint is needed.
extra: Initial release December 2024. Revision used is October 2025, not October 2026.

title: SafeVLA: Towards Safety Alignment of Vision-Language-Action Model via Constrained Learning
authors: Borong Zhang and Yuhao Zhang and Jiaming Ji and Yingshan Lei and Juntao Dai and Yuanpei Chen and Yaodong Yang
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38
summary: Uses constrained learning and targeted risk elicitation for VLA alignment, assessing safety-performance trade-offs, extreme failures, and distribution shifts in mobile manipulation.
gap: Safety and utility must be reported jointly, including tail failures. This is a relevant training-based comparison class, but retraining a general VLA is unnecessary for a focused runtime-interruption workshop study.

title: Generating Robot Constitutions & Benchmarks for Semantic Safety
authors: Pierre Sermanet and Anirudha Majumdar and Alex Irpan and Dmitry Kalashnikov and Vikas Sindhwani
summary: Introduces ASIMOV semantic-safety data grounded in visual situations and injury reports, together with generated robot constitutions for behavioral guidance.
gap: Useful for deriving interpretable hazards and semantic constraints. Agreement with a constitution does not establish that a recovery motion is dynamically feasible or physically harmless.

title: Can AI Perceive Physical Danger and Intervene?
authors: Abhishek Jindal and Dmitry Kalashnikov and R. Alex Hofer and Oscar Chang and Divya Garikapati and Anirudha Majumdar and Pierre Sermanet and Vikas Sindhwani
summary: Benchmarks perception of physical danger and intervention reasoning using images and videos grounded in injury narratives and operational constraints; it also explores safety-focused post-training.
gap: Recognizing danger is a necessary component. The proposed evaluation must execute the selected intervention and measure its physical outcome rather than relying on the model to judge its own safety.
extra: Distinct paper from [23], not a duplicate version of the same manuscript. Cited revision November 2025 is within cutoff.

title: Real-Time Out-of-Distribution Failure Prevention via Multi-Modal Reasoning
authors: Milan Ganai and Rohan Sinha and Christopher Agia and Daniel Morton and Luigi Di Lillo and Marco Pavone
summary: FORTRESS precomputes semantic fallback goals and safety representations, then performs dynamics-aware fallback planning. It evaluates semantic recognition and drone fallback execution and includes an example of replanning around moving concepts.
gap: Semantic fallback planning, caching, latency mitigation, and some dynamic replanning are already addressed. The distinct test is coupled contact-mode transitions, load retention, and bystander outcomes during humanoid interruption.
extra: Full-text Sections 4, 5, 7 and Appendix E checked. Avoid describing FORTRESS as purely static or as ignoring humans.
